subject: Immediate exec bridge: Dedicated pool exhaustion causing reserved throughput misses
body:
From: monitoring@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Alert: Dedicated pool us-west-2/rdw-dedicated-48 saturated (queued requests rising)

Alert summary:
- Pool: rdw-dedicated-48 (us-west-2)
- Symptom: sustained token queueing, 95th latency > 2.3s, 5xx spike to 1.7% for impacted reserved routes
- Affected customers: FidelityX (reserved qps 1200, observed throughput ~820)
- Runbook: start mitigation play 'dedicated-backoff-v2' and open ops bridge

Attachment: fidelityx_qps_graphs_20260915.png (image/png)

---

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Alert: Dedicated pool us-west-2/rdw-dedicated-48 saturated (queued requests rising)

Team —

FidelityX is hitting sustained headroom exhaustion on their reserved routes. Monitoring shows token queue depth creeping up over 30m and reserved throughput delivering ~68% of committed QPS. Customer is already reporting latency regressions in production. I tried the usual fast-fail backoff and routing to hot-standby but their traffic is pinned to reserved pool.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you open an ops bridge and invite customer? (they want visibility)
- Vivek: can we evaluate short-term headroom reallocation from non-reserved pools (manual route override) — detail impact and rollback plan
- Aditya: confirm whether any ongoing deployment/eviction in us-west-2 this morning that could explain sudden kernel saturation

I'll loop in CS and account. If this persists, we'll need an exec bridge to prioritize mitigation and decide on temporary > committed throttle allowances.

-Jasmine
Product Sales
Redwood Inference

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, chad.jensen@fidelityx.com, ops@fidelityx.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Alert: Dedicated pool us-west-2/rdw-dedicated-48 saturated (queued requests rising)

Opened bridge: https://zoom.company/ops-bridge/rdw-4816 (invites sent)

What I can share from the bridge so far:
- Ops: kernel-level telemetry shows elevated GPU SM utilization and NVLINK saturation on 3 nodes in the pool; processes are not being OOM'd but queueing persists
- SRE suggested temporarily moving non-critical customers to a lower-cost shared pool to free headroom for reserved lanes
- CS (on call): Chad from FidelityX is on the bridge; they confirm they see degraded response times and some 429s when they spike beyond bursts

Temporary mitigation proposals on the bridge:
1) Emergency headroom borrow: reassign 6 GPUs from lower-priority non-reserved cluster (manual routing) — projected to restore FidelityX to ~95% committed throughput within 8–12 minutes; rollback cost: increased latency for moved tenants (~10–15% increase).
2) Short-term QoS throttle: enforce stricter prefix caching + per-request early rejection at 90% of reserved QPS to stop queue growth and avoid 5xx cascade (may degrade customer-perceived throughput).
3) Model fallback: switch FidelityX route to the lighter quantized variant (same quality profile) — requires 2–3 minute rollout and some telemetry validation.

Customer asks for clarity on timeline and whether this will impact their SLA credit exposure.

---

From: chad.jensen@fidelityx.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ops@fidelityx.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alert: Dedicated pool us-west-2/rdw-dedicated-48 saturated (queued requests rising)

Marissa / Jasmine —
Thanks for the quick bridge. To be direct: we are running a revenue-critical feature during a customer event today. Any sustained shortfalls hit our top-line. We need a firm remediation timeline and confirmation that you won't pause our traffic or route us to a lower-quality model without prior consent. If borrowing headroom is the fastest path, we need to know which customers will be impacted and for how long.

-Chad
VP Engineering, FidelityX

---

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Alert: Dedicated pool us-west-2/rdw-dedicated-48 saturated (queued requests rising)

Quick technical readout:
- Cause: sustained traffic pattern (burst window) combined with an inefficient kernel path on the latest optimized build; we have a transient regression in batching behavior for sequence-lengths ~1–30 tokens which FidelityX heavily uses for microcalls.
- Evidence: profiler + KV hit-rate traces attached in bridge notes (see confluence link).
- Immediate actions I triggered:
  * Manual routing override prepared (can shift 6 GPUs from non-reserved cluster f-west-2-lowprio)
  * Hot rollback of the kernel optimization patch for rdw-dedicated-48 queued (requires 10–12 min to restart 3 nodes sequentially)
  * Canary of quantized variant prepared, but we're holding until customer signs off

Recommendation (first 2 hours): borrow headroom + rollback patch. This minimizes customer impact and avoids throttling. We should prepare an internal exec sync to OK cross-tenant headroom borrow.

Vivek
Sr. SRE Lead

---

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, chad.jensen@fidelityx.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Immediate exec bridge: Dedicated pool exhaustion causing reserved throughput misses

Summary + exec asks: 
1) We're executing Vivek's recommendation now: manual headroom reassign beginning 17:10 PT — expected restoration to ~95% of committed QPS within 12 minutes.
2) Aditya to approve the kernel rollback window (rolling restart of 3 nodes) at 17:25 PT; this will be communicated to affected tenants in the non-reserved cluster.
3) Marissa to coordinate CS message and a short customer FAQ explaining the short-term headroom borrow and SLA implications — propose we offer a one-week service credit if throughput drops below committed during this window.
4) Prio: if headroom borrow is blocked by leadership, we need an immediate exec bridge (CTO + Head of SRE) to approve temporary cross-tenant reallocations.

Chad — we're prioritizing FidelityX; you'll get an update within 20 minutes and a post-mortem within 48 hours.

Action items in Confluence: https://redwood-confluence.internal/incident/FID-8921 (runbook + timeline link)
Attachments: requested_runbook_patch.diff (text/plain)

-Jasmine
Product Sales
Redwood Inference
